title_en: Children and Their Rights in Islam
summary: Islam establishes comprehensive rights for children from before birth, covering their right to life, proper naming, education, maintenance, emotional care, and a sound religious upbringing. The Prophet ﷺ demonstrated exceptional tenderness toward children and the Quran frames their protection as a fundamental parental and societal obligation.
content:
## Children Before Birth: The Right to Life

Allah forbade the pre-Islamic practice of killing children — particularly daughters — out of poverty or shame: 'And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for them and for you. Indeed, their killing is ever a great sin.' (Surah al-Isra', 17:31)

'And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked, for what sin she was killed.' (Surah al-Takwir, 81:8–9) — The Quran condemns female infanticide as a crime that will be called to account on the Day of Judgment.

## The Right to a Good Name

The Prophet ﷺ said: 'It is your duty to give your children good names.' (Sunan Abu Dawud, Hadith 4948; graded hasan)

He changed unfavourable names and encouraged names that carry good meanings, particularly names of the prophets and those with praise of Allah (Abdullah, Abdurrahman).

## The Right to Aqiqah

On the seventh day after birth, it is recommended (per Shafi'i and Hanbali) or sunnah mu'akkadah to slaughter: two sheep for a boy and one for a girl, name the child, and shave the head. (Sunan Abu Dawud, Hadith 2837; graded sahih)

## The Right to Breastfeeding and Early Nurture

The Quran establishes the right to breastfeeding: 'Mothers may nurse their children two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing.' (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:233)

The father bears the cost of nursing even if separated from the mother.

## The Right to Education and Tarbiyah

The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Command your children to pray at seven, and discipline them for it at ten, and separate them in their beds.' (Sunan Abu Dawud, Hadith 495; graded hasan sahih)

Parents are obligated to teach their children the foundations of Islam, Quranic recitation, the obligations of worship, and good character (akhlaq).

## The Right to Financial Maintenance

Fathers are obligated to financially provide for their children's food, clothing, shelter, and education until they reach maturity (bulugh) and independence. This applies even after divorce — the father maintains financial responsibility for his children regardless of custodial arrangements.

## The Right to Just Treatment Among Siblings

The Prophet ﷺ prohibited favouritism in gifts among children: 'Fear Allah and treat your children equally.' (Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 2587; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 1623) — A parent who gifts one child must give equally to all, or not give at all.

## The Prophet ﷺ with Children

The Prophet ﷺ demonstrated extraordinary tenderness:
- He prolonged his prostration when his grandson Hasan رضي الله عنه climbed on his back: 'My grandson made me a horse and I was happy to be one.' (Musnad Ahmad)
- He shortened his prayer when he heard a child crying so as not to distress the mother
- He played with children, greeted them first, and called them by kind nicknames
- Anas ibn Malik رضي الله عنه served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years and reported: 'He never said "uff" to me, never said "why did you do this" or "why did you not do that".' (Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2309)
evidence_hadith: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 2587 — treat children equally in gifts
Sunan Abu Dawud, Hadith 495 — command prayer at seven
Sunan Abu Dawud, Hadith 4948 — give children good names
Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2309 — Anas's testimony about the Prophet's gentleness
sources: Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni (sections on children's maintenance)
Al-Ghazali, Ihya Ulum al-Din (section on tarbiyah)
